name: Recoverable Form
purpose: Collect or edit meaningful input with clear grouping, honest save state and a recovery route that retains valid user work.
useWhen: A user creates, edits or submits a meaningful record.
Errors, server rejection or interrupted saving must be recoverable.
avoidWhen: Content is read-only or the task only changes a collection query.
A binary immediate toggle needs no extended data-entry workflow.

states.presentation: Show record identity, editable scope and required/optional convention.

states.meaning: Input differs from confirmed saved state.
states.presentation: Show unsaved status without repeated announcements.
Label saving, prevent duplicate requests and keep entered values visible.

states.meaning: Client or server rejected one or more values.
states.presentation: Persistent summary links and field-specific correction text.

states.meaning: Save failed or result is unknown.
states.presentation: Show persistent retry or verify-outcome action; never claim success.
Confirm outcome with record identity and saved status.
Offer stay, save where possible and explicit discard.

transitions.guard: Local validation passes; otherwise use invalid state.

transitions.focus: Focus the safe Stay choice in the named confirmation.
Retain save focus or move to next task only for explicit navigation intent.
Focus summary on submitted multi-field failure; links reveal and focus invalid controls.
Keep submit focus; expose persistent recovery.
Keep the corrected control; remove obsolete error after revalidation.
Keep submit focus after corrected validation.

transitions.guard: Verify unknown outcome or use an application-owned idempotency policy before retry.

transitions.focus: Keep edited value and server revision.
Return to initiating field or navigation trigger.
Navigate only after explicit discard; destination owns focus.

visual.hierarchy: Task and entity identity lead; group headings organize decisions; labels stay closer to controls than adjacent groups.
visual.alignment: Use a shared label and input axis; align action group with form content rather than the outer viewport.
visual.spacing: Keep hint and error adjacent to their input, with larger space between task groups; reserve error space only when it avoids disruptive jumps.
visual.typography: Body-size inputs and labels remain readable; hints and optional markers use a quieter but legible supporting role.
visual.emphasis: Save is the strongest task action; cancel and destructive actions have distinct subordinate placement.
visual.surfaces: Use section whitespace or restrained dividers; avoid boxing each field into a competing surface.
visual.proportions: Choose input widths by expected value and allow long labels to wrap; avoid a full-width short numeric field suggesting long content.
visual.discoverability: Keep submit outcome and save scope visible; reveal advanced inputs with a named disclosure rather than hidden gesture.
visual.states: Show invalidity with correction text and an additional visual marker; distinguish unsaved, saving, unknown outcome and confirmed saved.
visual.brand: Use existing field, error and action tokens; brand adaptation must preserve error readability and focus visibility.

keyboard.result: Follow task order with persistent visible focus; no layout-only positive tabindex.
keyboard.focus: Each labeled control or disclosure button.

keyboard.when: Submit intent outside multiline text or specialized controls.
keyboard.result: Validate current values without bypassing server checks.
keyboard.focus: Summary after failed submission; otherwise retain submit.

keyboard.when: An error-summary link or section disclosure.
keyboard.result: Reveal the relevant section and focus the exact invalid field.
keyboard.focus: Named invalid control; preserve values in all other fields.

keyboard.result: Choose Stay when dismissal is allowed.
keyboard.focus: Return to the originating control; do not silently discard.

accessibility.naming: Give the region a task-specific heading and each control a persistent name.
accessibility.semantics: Use form, fieldset, legend and associated visible labels. Required state is programmatically exposed; hints and errors reference controls, invalid state follows validation. A failed submit exposes a focusable linked summary; server-level failures remain persistent and announced without clearing inputs.

checks.requirement: Every task and recovery action can be completed with keyboard input.
checks.passEvidence: Record the starting focus, complete the task and verify a visible logical destination.

responsive.condition: Fields or actions no longer fit readable columns, including narrow, tablet, enlarged text or short usable viewport.
responsive.restructure: Stack related fields in reading order. For an overlay, give its body one vertical scroll owner constrained by the usable viewport; keep Save/Cancel reachable without clipping and reveal focused inputs/errors above any sticky actions. Use native scrollbar auto by default, not global overflow locking.
responsive.focusContinuity: Retain the same field across resize. Error links reveal the containing section and scroll the target clear of fixed chrome; close returns to the invoker.

responsive.condition: The page or another overlay already owns scrolling.
responsive.restructure: Choose page editing or one modal focus owner deliberately; avoid simultaneously scrolling form, dialog and page for the same task. A temporary modal background lock must be scoped, preserve page position and restore scrolling on every exit.
responsive.focusContinuity: Test Tab and Shift+Tab, Escape and error focus in a short viewport; do not treat a transient BODY stop alone as proof of background control access.

density.useWhen: Mixed input methods, occasional use or unfamiliar terminology.
constraints: Keep controls independently reachable without overlapping hit areas.
Allow user text sizing and wrapping to determine minimum row or field height.

density.useWhen: Repeated scanning by experienced operators with a measured information need.
constraints: Reduce surrounding padding before reducing readable text size.
Preserve focus outline clearance, labels and distinct control targets.

motion.purpose: Explain a local state change without interrupting the current task.
motion.trigger: User initiated disclosure or result replacement.
motion.reduced: Replace content immediately; keep textual progress and completion feedback.
motion.interruption: Cancel obsolete transitions; never queue animation behind new input or block retry.

recovery.explanation: Map server field keys to visible input errors; retain unknown/global errors in summary.
Preserve input; distinguish known rejection from unknown completion and verify outcome before repeating consequential work.

checks.requirement: Long labels, absent values and permission restrictions remain distinguishable.
checks.passEvidence: Inspect narrow and wide views with synthetic long labels and missing data.

checks.requirement: Failure preserves user intent and exposes an operable next step.
checks.passEvidence: Inject failure, retry and confirm identity, entered values and focus remain coherent.

checks.requirement: Failure when ordinary page content produces unintended horizontal overflow; a declared two-dimensional comparison region is evaluated separately.
checks.passEvidence: At 375, 768 and 1440 CSS px and enlarged text, measure document width and locate the offending node; repair its layout instead of globally clipping overflow.

checks.requirement: Review each genuinely overflowing region for a perceptible cue or reachable alternative control, plus keyboard and touch access.
checks.passEvidence: Record axis, task, accessible name, focus path and cue/control; test keyboard scrolling or equivalent navigation and swipe. Hidden scrollbar alone is neither pass nor failure.

checks.requirement: Review multiple scroll owners; unnecessary same-axis nesting can strand focus, wheel or touch input.
checks.passEvidence: Inventory page, collection, filter and dialog scroll owners; justify containment per task and exercise boundaries. Region count alone cannot determine a failure.

checks.requirement: Failure when a layout change loses the focused record/field, enters a hidden duplicate or changes keyboard task order incoherently.
checks.passEvidence: Resize with a field or row action focused; preserve identity, draft/query and logical order, then complete the task in both Tab directions.

checks.requirement: Failure when Save/Cancel or a focused correction cannot be brought into the usable dialog viewport.
checks.passEvidence: At 375 by 500 CSS px, then simulated reduced visual viewport, reach inputs/errors and Save/Cancel by keyboard and scroll; check occlusion by footer, preserve draft on resize and restore page position on exit.

anatomy.purpose: Distinguish unsaved, pending and confirmed success.

variants.useWhen: A small or medium task can be completed in one coherent page.
guidance: Order identity and required decisions before optional detail; indicate optional and required fields consistently.

variants.useWhen: Long entry benefits from task sections and progressive disclosure.
guidance: Keep progress and save scope explicit; reveal the containing section before focusing a hidden invalid field.
Preserve values in collapsed or previous sections and show unresolved errors in the summary.

composition.focusOwner: Form owns validation focus; workspace coordinates detail dismissal and return to record.
